title: Coupling Language Models with Physics-based Simulation for Synthesis of Inorganic Materials
experiments_summary: The study establishes a hybrid evaluation framework for inorganic synthesis planning using the binary niobium-oxygen (Nb-O) system as a case study. Equilibrium phase fractions were computed via the CALPHAD technique using PyCalphad and the Pérez-Massih thermodynamic database at 10 K intervals from 300 K to 3000 K with 1 at.% compositional spacing. Kinetics were approximated using a Johnson-Mehl-Avrami (JMA) model with an activation energy of 95.4 kJ/mol and a pre-exponential factor k0 = 100 s⁻¹ calibrated to reproduce the Nb-to-Nb2O5 oxidation timescale at 900 K. Four synthesis challenge problems of varying complexity were designed, each specifying a starting state and a goal state (defined as phase fractions plus temperature at 1 bar), requiring combinations of precursor addition (Nb or O2), temperature changes (300–3000 K), and wait steps. Two planning approaches were compared: (1) A* search with the state space discretized into 100 bins per dimension (phase fraction, element fraction, temperature), using path length as cost and normalized Euclidean distance as heuristic; and (2) a ReAct-based LLM agent implemented in DSPy using GPT-4o (temperature setting 0.1) with access to the physics simulator as a callable tool. The LLM was run ten times per challenge to account for stochastic variability, while A* was run once due to its deterministic nature. A* was allowed to run until a solution was found or 128 GB RAM was exhausted. Success was defined as reaching within an approximate ε-ball of the goal state, with unresponsive solutions (final temperature deviating >20 K from goal) assigned maximum error of 1.0; otherwise scoring used scaled mean squared error between goal and realized phase fractions. Additionally, DSPy's LabeledFewShot prompt tuning strategy was applied to the LLM, randomly sampling k=4 training examples to augment the prompt, and pre- versus post-tuning LLM performance distributions were compared across all four challenges.
